inspection_summary: Inspected all 4,267 normalized lines of the 1916 Hardy-Littlewood memoir. The source contains a dense chain of Mellin-transform and Tauberian arguments, explicit formulas over zeta and Dirichlet L-function zeros, conditional oscillation results, a mean-square calculation, oscillatory zero-sum estimates, a critical-line sign-change method, and a Diophantine phase-alignment proof of prime-counting oscillations. Prose and theorem structure are generally recoverable, but many displayed formulas are degraded by PDF extraction and require comparison with the retained scan before exact symbolic reuse.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and introduction/summary
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the paper's problem families, previews the transform/Tauberian, zero-sum, critical-line, and prime-oscillation mechanisms, and records limitations and unsuccessful strengthenings.

sections_inspected.label: 2.1 The prime number theorem and allied theorems
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops Cahen-Mellin plus Tauberian transfer from analytic continuation and growth of generalized Dirichlet series to coefficient-sum asymptotics, including prime-number-theorem applications.

sections_inspected.label: 2.2 The function sum (mu(n)-1)e^{-ny}
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives an explicit residue formula, controls its zero contribution under RH, proves two-sided oscillation, and compares exponential smoothing with Riesz/Cesaro means.

sections_inspected.label: 2.3 On an assertion of Tschebyschef
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transforms a prime-residue bias into a Dirichlet L-zero formula, obtains a conditional one-sided divergence, and studies its first-order means.

sections_inspected.label: 2.4 Mean value of |zeta(1/2+it)|^2
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses Mellin-Bessel transforms, divisor sums, asymptotic localization, and an integral Tauberian lemma to derive the critical-line mean square.

sections_inspected.label: 2.5 Ramanujan-Riesz reciprocal series and RH criterion
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Presents conjectural reciprocal-transform identities, isolates the missing contour estimate, generalizes through reciprocal functions, and derives a Riesz-function growth criterion for RH.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Weighted exponential series over zeta zeros
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Adapts Landau's contour method and stationary-phase analysis to weighted oscillatory sums over zero ordinates, with uniformity and convergence regimes.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Zeros of zeta on the critical line
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proves sign changes of a real critical-line auxiliary function in short intervals and obtains a lower bound for the number of critical-line zeros.

sections_inspected.label: 5 Order of psi(x)-x and Pi(x)-Li(x)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Combines an explicit zero formula, phase alignment, a boundary maximum-principle lemma, and smoothed-to-sharp transfer to prove large oscillations in prime-counting errors.

sections_inspected.label: Additional note and erratum
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Records independent later work overlapping Section 4 and an unrelated correction; contains no new proof mechanism for this source plan.

accepted_units.title: Cahen-Mellin plus Tauberian transfer to prime-number-theorem equivalents
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction identifies a reusable architecture: convert a generalized Dirichlet series by Mellin inversion, then use one-sided Tauberian hypotheses to recover coefficient-sum asymptotics and several elementarily equivalent forms of the prime number theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the authors' definition of elementary equivalence and the asymptotic notation needed to read the previewed claims.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed formulas are partially degraded; the prose, labels, and equivalence claim are clear, but exact transcription should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Smoothed Möbius explicit formula and RH-conditioned oscillation
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces the exponentially smoothed arithmetic error, forecasts an explicit zero formula, and separates an RH-sized upper bound and two-sided oscillation from the stronger estimates the method cannot reach.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the comparison with the sharp Chebyshev error and the stated obstruction to treating a related weighted prime sum.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The defining sum and inequalities are OCR-damaged; prose makes the mechanism recoverable, while exact symbols require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Tschebyschef prime-bias assertion through a Dirichlet L-function
accepted_units.why_material: Frames a prime-residue bias as a transform governed by zeros of a Dirichlet L-function and explicitly distinguishes the proved implication under the critical-line hypothesis from the unproved converse intuition.
accepted_units.context_note: The span is a self-contained statement of the assertion, analytic hypothesis, and failure mode.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The alternating prime series and L-series are legible only approximately in extraction; exact signs and exponents need the scan.

accepted_units.title: Weighted exponential sums over zero ordinates
accepted_units.why_material: Explains how Landau's zero-power-sum method is adapted to damped oscillatory sums and highlights a potentially artificial parameter dependence in the proved order estimate.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the RH simplification, the model exponential sum, the theorem preview, and the authors' sharper conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several central displayed series are missing or garbled; prose preserves the representation change and conjectural comparison, but exact bounds require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: From special-function proofs to short-interval sign changes on the critical line
accepted_units.why_material: Tracks how an existence proof using Mellin and theta-function behavior was simplified and then replaced by a different sign-change argument yielding a zero in every sufficiently long short interval, while recording an unsuccessful stronger density target.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains the historical baseline, the method dependencies removed, the improved conclusion, and the failed extension.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose is clear; the exact exponents in the interval and counting bound are extraction-sensitive and should be verified from the scan.

accepted_units.title: Why persistent empirical prime-counting bias must eventually reverse
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts a slowly varying fixed-sign contribution with a larger oscillatory zero contribution and previews Kronecker-style simultaneous phase alignment, explaining both long empirical bias and inevitable reversals.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes extensions to weighted prime sums and primes in competing residue classes, exposing the generality of the mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual prose is reliable; exact normalization and displayed orders are OCR-damaged and need scan checking.

accepted_units.title: Mellin inversion, Fourier decay, and one-sided Tauberian recovery
accepted_units.why_material: Packages three reusable steps: exponential-kernel Mellin inversion, decay of an integrable vertical-line transform, and recovery of partial sums from small-parameter exponential asymptotics under controlled coefficient increments.
accepted_units.context_note: These lemmas supply the full interface used by the following Dirichlet-series theorems.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula layout is degraded, especially the coefficient hypotheses; scan verification is required for exact statement reuse.

accepted_units.title: Analytic continuation and vertical growth imply small exponential sums and partial sums
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how contour displacement turns continuation and vertical growth of a generalized Dirichlet series into an o(y^{-c}) exponential-sum bound, then invokes the Tauberian lemma to obtain o(lambda_n^c) partial sums.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes theorem hypotheses, the contour shift, the decay lemma, and the coefficient-sum corollary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The proof strategy is clear from prose and labels; exact Gamma factors and inequalities need the scan.

accepted_units.title: The c=0 boundary yields convergence at the analytic value
accepted_units.why_material: Modifies the shifted contour at the boundary c=0 by indenting around the origin, converting regularity there into ordinary convergence of coefficients and deriving a Möbius-series consequence.
accepted_units.context_note: The semicircular indentation and limiting calculation are retained because they distinguish this case from the positive-c theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The contour description is clear, but the displayed integral and example series require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A simple pole becomes the main coefficient-sum term
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces boundary regularity by a simple pole and shows that its residue becomes the leading asymptotic after Mellin inversion and Tauberian recovery, with the prime number theorem as the principal instance.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the modified explicit formula, the asymptotic transfer, and the logarithmic-derivative specialization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact constants and the zeta logarithmic derivative are formula-dependent and must be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Removing an artificial vertical-growth restriction by changing the kernel
accepted_units.why_material: Separates genuine hypotheses from proof artifacts, notes a failure for rapidly spaced exponents, and removes the restrictive growth exponent by replacing the exponential kernel with a fractional-power kernel and transferring back to the original scale.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes comparison with Landau, a counter-regime, the conjectured artifact, and the rescaling argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The rescaled Mellin identities and exponent arithmetic are OCR-sensitive; the prose makes the repair mechanism clear, but exact formulas need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Contour displacement and complete residue taxonomy for a smoothed Möbius sum
accepted_units.why_material: Builds an explicit formula by moving the Mellin contour and classifying contributions from the main pole, the origin, nontrivial zeros, trivial zeros, and double poles, including an explicit warning about the delicate limiting justification.
accepted_units.context_note: The retained footnote distinguishes a genuinely nontrivial contour-limit step from the residue bookkeeping.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Residue formulas are substantially degraded in extraction; the pole taxonomy and analytic structure are clear, but scan verification is mandatory for exact use.

accepted_units.title: Subtracting the Bernoulli expansion isolates the zero sum
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a second Mellin representation for the unweighted exponential sum and subtracts it from the Möbius formula, leaving a zero-driven term plus controlled analytic power-series remainders.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the decisive representation change from arithmetic coefficients to spectral zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed equations are OCR-damaged; the subtraction and analytic-remainder claim are explicit in prose, but coefficients require the scan.

accepted_units.title: Crude local zero counts suffice to control the RH zero tail
accepted_units.why_material: Under RH, reorganizes positive zero ordinates and shows that a deliberately crude zero-count bound is enough to make the discarded tail smaller than the leading pair of zero terms.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves the contrast between a sharp known local count and the much weaker numerical inequality actually needed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The numerical bounds and decomposition are formula-dependent and should be verified from the scan.

accepted_units.title: First zero pair forces two-sided square-root oscillation
accepted_units.why_material: Combines the explicit formula and tail estimate to obtain an RH-sized upper bound and infinitely recurring positive and negative values, then transfers this to the sharp Chebyshev error and records why an off-line zero does not yet yield the analogous smoothed statement.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the theorem, its arithmetic corollary, and the failed stronger inference when RH is false.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact Omega notation and constants are extraction-sensitive; the direction and scope of every claim are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Riesz/Cesaro means restore regularity lost by the sharp sum
accepted_units.why_material: Explains that the exponential smoothing behaves as regularly as the zeros allow whereas the sharp sum does not, then derives comparable bounds for every positive-order Riesz/Cesaro mean and distinguishes Abelian implications in each direction.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the motivation, integral representation, zero expansion, theorem, and the asymmetric logical comparison with the previous result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Many displayed definitions and the final bound are garbled; scan verification is needed for exact mean normalization and exponents.

accepted_units.title: Prime-residue bias expressed as a sum over Dirichlet L-zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Expands the logarithmic derivative of the relevant Dirichlet L-function, applies Mellin inversion, and shifts the contour to express the weighted bias through its complex zeros plus analytic remainders.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains the original assertion, the critical-line assumption, and the full transform setup.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prime signs, powers, and the transformed integrand are OCR-sensitive; the prose and equation labels recover the architecture only.

accepted_units.title: Completed L-function product bounds the aggregate zero contribution
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the functional equation to form a real even completed function, factors it over real zero ordinates, and extracts a coefficient identity giving both a global reciprocal-square sum and a lower bound on the first zero.
accepted_units.context_note: This replaces the cruder local zero-count argument used for zeta with a product identity tailored to the L-function.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The completed function and coefficient identity are badly extracted; exact products and constants require the scan.

accepted_units.title: Separating prime, prime-square, and higher-power terms exposes one-sided bias
accepted_units.why_material: Bounds the total zero contribution, decomposes the logarithmic-derivative coefficients by prime-power multiplicity, and shows the prime-square main term dominates the higher-power remainder, forcing the prime contribution negative.
accepted_units.context_note: The decomposition is retained through the resulting conditional theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed decomposition and constants need scan verification; the prose identifies each component and the dominance relation.

accepted_units.title: Fractional coefficient weighting preserves a one-sided lower bound
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces an integral transform that turns a lower bound for an exponential generating function into a lower bound after multiplying coefficients by n^{-s}, with an explicit restriction on the exponent range.
accepted_units.context_note: This abstract transfer is used immediately to prepare the convergence factor needed for the original prime-bias assertion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Kernel normalization and exponents are formula-dependent and require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A logarithmic convergence factor proves Tschebyschef's assertion under the L-hypothesis
accepted_units.why_material: Represents 1/log n by an integral kernel, transfers the one-sided bound to the prime series, and obtains the claimed divergence rate; it also states the compelling but unproved reason the assertion should fail if the L-zero hypothesis fails.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the kernel asymptotic, theorem, conditional conclusion, and precise oscillatory-term obstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The rate and kernel equations are OCR-damaged and must be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: First-order Riesz/Cesaro means yield a stronger averaged prime bias
accepted_units.why_material: Recasts the bias in Riesz means, isolates prime, square, and higher-power contributions again, and obtains a first-order mean tending to negative infinity, from which the earlier exponential assertions follow Abelianly.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the comparison of mean orders and the explicit link back to the unsmoothed Section 5 phenomena.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mean definitions and orders are extraction-sensitive; the structural comparison is clear, but exact formulas require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Bessel-Mellin and integral Tauberian lemmas for the zeta mean square
accepted_units.why_material: States the missing critical-line mean-square asymptotic and assembles a Mellin-square identity, a sectorial Bessel asymptotic, and an integral Tauberian theorem that will convert a damped transform into cumulative mean behavior.
accepted_units.context_note: The three lemmas form a coherent proof interface rather than isolated facts.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The target constant and kernel formulas are OCR-degraded; exact statements need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Divisor-weighted Bessel transform localizes the zeta mean square
accepted_units.why_material: Sums the Mellin-Bessel kernel with divisor coefficients, moves the contour through a double pole, uses the functional equation, and chooses a near-boundary angle so the resulting series has a tractable localized asymptotic.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes residue extraction, the complex rotation, dismissal of negligible terms, and the final damped asymptotic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Most displayed formulas are heavily degraded; the prose preserves the contour and localization mechanism, but scan verification is mandatory.

accepted_units.title: Damped mean-square asymptotics imply the undamped critical-line mean square
accepted_units.why_material: Applies the integral Tauberian lemma to the localized transform, then uses a change of variables and integration by parts to recover the asymptotic for the cumulative square modulus of zeta.
accepted_units.context_note: This closes the proof chain begun in the preceding two units.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed constants and intermediate integrals are damaged; exact theorem transcription requires the scan.

accepted_units.title: Ramanujan-inspired reciprocal formula from a non-rigorous contour shift
accepted_units.why_material: Derives a striking reciprocity between a Möbius-Gaussian series at reciprocal parameters by Mellin inversion and a proposed contour shift across zeta zeros, then checks the symmetry constraint on the residue series.
accepted_units.context_note: The authors explicitly deny having a satisfactory proof, so this is retained as a failed-route/strategic-hypothesis unit rather than an established theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Central formulas are severely OCR-damaged and the argument is conditional; scan verification is essential even for the conjectural statement.

accepted_units.title: The missing horizontal-boundary estimate and reciprocal-function generalization
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies a concrete sufficient zeta bound along a sequence of heights or curves that would justify the contour shift, admits the inability to prove it even under RH, and generalizes the reciprocal structure through paired cosine transforms and Mellin factors.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes what can be shown by bracketing and why that remains insufficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The required inequality and transform equations are OCR-sensitive; prose clearly states the logical gap and generalization.

accepted_units.title: Functional equations propagate reciprocal identities and conditional growth
accepted_units.why_material: Combines reciprocal-transform functional equations with the zeta and Gamma functional equations to produce a broader family of candidate identities, then shows how RH plus absolute convergence would impose square-root-scale growth.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the return to the original Riesz function and the conditional order inference.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed identities are largely missing in extraction; exact symbolic content requires the scan.

accepted_units.title: Riesz-function growth as a necessary and sufficient criterion for RH
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a Mellin integral for the Riesz function to motivate a growth criterion, explains why analytic continuation would imply RH, then proves the converse estimate from a known RH consequence for Möbius partial sums.
accepted_units.context_note: Separates the heuristic route to the criterion from the later proof of necessity and sufficiency.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact growth exponent and Mellin quotient are extraction-sensitive; scan verification is required.

accepted_units.title: Weighted damped exponential sums over zeta zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Starts from Landau's resonance formula, converts it under RH to an exponential sum in zero ordinates, and states uniform bounds and convergence regimes for a damped and rotated generalization.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes why RH is simplifying rather than essential and the full parameter regime of the target theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The central series and exponents are OCR-damaged; prose and labels preserve the setup but exact theorem use needs the scan.

accepted_units.title: Partial summation reduces the rotation parameter to the base case
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that proving the theorem at zero rotation suffices, using partial summation to transfer a uniform base bound to the general oscillatory factor.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the uniformity requirement that is maintained through the rest of the section.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exponent bookkeeping is formula-dependent and needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A rectangular zero-residue contour isolates a difficult top edge
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs a large rectangle for the logarithmic derivative, lets the far-left edge recede, decomposes the top edge into far-zero and near-zero pieces, and proves all but the main vertical integral negligible.
accepted_units.context_note: The local decomposition of zeta'/zeta near ordinates is retained because it prevents zero proximity from invalidating the contour bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour integrals and exponents are heavily degraded; scan verification is required for exact estimates.

accepted_units.title: The main contour integral becomes a Dirichlet-series oscillatory integral
accepted_units.why_material: Reduces the surviving vertical integral to a Dirichlet series whose coefficient terms are oscillatory integrals, then partitions indices according to whether the phase has an interior stationary point.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the bridge from complex contour estimates to real stationary-phase analysis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact phase and weights are formula-sensitive and need the scan.

accepted_units.title: Monotone-phase integration controls both tails uniformly
accepted_units.why_material: Proves an integration lemma after the change of variable w=t log(t/xi), then applies it symmetrically to indices below and above the stationary range to bound both nonstationary tails.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the elementary monotonicity argument and its two tail applications.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Denominators and exponent bounds are OCR-degraded; exact constants require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Local quadratic expansion at the phase critical point
accepted_units.why_material: Locates the stationary point, rescales around it, separates central and outer pieces with careful endpoint conventions, and obtains the main Gaussian/Fresnel-scale estimate from a quadratic phase expansion.
accepted_units.context_note: The exceptional endpoint cases are retained because they show how the decomposition remains uniform.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The central asymptotic formulas are badly extracted; prose preserves the scaling and decomposition, but scan verification is mandatory.

accepted_units.title: Five error sums close the weighted zero-sum estimate
accepted_units.why_material: Substitutes the stationary-phase bounds into the coefficient sum, estimates five distinct error families, and recombines them with the contour reduction and RH parameterization to prove the section's theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the aggregation because it records which local errors survive summation and which parameter inequalities make them negligible.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Almost every displayed estimate is OCR-sensitive; exact exponent verification requires the scan.

accepted_units.title: Critical-line zeros from sign changes of a real auxiliary function
accepted_units.why_material: Defines a real-valued critical-line auxiliary function and reduces the existence of an odd-order zero in each short interval to two integral estimates, explicitly separating the easy contradiction stage from the hard cancellation stage.

accepted_units.why_material: Assuming the auxiliary function keeps one sign, converts its absolute integral into a zeta integral and uses a rectangle plus the functional equation to expose a main term too large for the previously asserted cancellation bound.

accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour vertices and powers are extraction-sensitive and require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Bounding side edges reduces critical-line cancellation to one short vertical integral
accepted_units.why_material: Uses another rectangle and uniform zeta/Gamma bounds to dismiss two sides, leaving a single short vertical integral as the only remaining estimate needed for sign changes.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains the exact reduction interface used by the oscillatory-sum analysis that follows.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The integrand and exponents are OCR-damaged; exact bounds need the scan.

accepted_units.title: At most one resonant Dirichlet term controls the short-interval integral
accepted_units.why_material: Applies Stirling's formula, freezes slow factors, expands into oscillatory Dirichlet terms, and splits around the unique possible stationary index; nonresonant terms are bounded by the earlier phase lemma and the central finite block is controlled directly.
accepted_units.context_note: This reuses Section 3's phase analysis in a new proof context and completes the hard cancellation stage.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The formula extraction is poor; exact phases, powers, and final estimates require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Odd-order critical-line zero in every prescribed short interval
accepted_units.why_material: Records the source's final local sign-change theorem and its global lower bound for the number of critical-line zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Kept separately from the proof to preserve the precise output of the mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The interval and counting exponents are OCR-sensitive and should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Prime-error oscillation reduced to a sine series over zero ordinates
accepted_units.why_material: States the target two-sided Omega bounds, notes why RH may be assumed without loss for this lower-bound goal, and uses the zero-counting inverse plus the explicit formula to express the normalized prime error as a convergent sine series.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains both the sharp arithmetic target and the spectral representation used to reach it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The explicit formula and normalizations are OCR-damaged; exact statements require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A damped zero series has a logarithmically large boundary profile
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces an analytic damping parameter, approximates zero ordinates through the inverse counting function, converts the sum into a tractable integral, and obtains an explicit large asymptotic along a shrinking interior path.
accepted_units.context_note: This constructs the seed large value that phase alignment and boundary transfer will amplify.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The defining series and constants are formula-sensitive; the derivation is recoverable from prose but exact use requires the scan.

accepted_units.title: Tail control plus simultaneous approximation moves the large value deep into the strip
accepted_units.why_material: Controls the high-zero tail uniformly, uses Dirichlet/Kronecker-style simultaneous approximation to align finitely many zero phases with the seed configuration, and obtains arbitrarily high strip points carrying logarithmically large imaginary part.

accepted_units.why_material: Explains why the standard theorem cannot be applied to the boundary zero series, formulates a strip maximum-principle variant with only pointwise boundary limits plus local boundedness, and proves it by damping with an auxiliary entire factor and splitting the rectangle.

accepted_units.title: Interior Omega behavior forces boundary Omega behavior

accepted_units.title: From Chebyshev oscillations to prime-counting oscillations using smoothed control
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the main Chebyshev-error oscillation theorem and then shows why ordinary partial summation is insufficient for one-sided Omega relations; a prime-power aggregate and the earlier Riesz/Cesaro bound control the extra term, yielding oscillations of Pi(x)-Li(x).

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Kernel choice separates analytic input from Tauberian recovery
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Across regular, boundary, pole, and excessive-growth cases, the source repeatedly factors an argument into Mellin-kernel contour information and a separate Tauberian coefficient-recovery step; changing the kernel can remove a proof-induced growth restriction without changing the intended arithmetic conclusion.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact admissible exponent ranges and coefficient hypotheses are formula-dependent and require scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Smoothing reveals a spectrum between zero-regularity and sharp arithmetic irregularity
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Exponential, Riesz, and Cesaro smoothing make zero-driven scale bounds accessible, while the sharp summatory functions can oscillate more strongly; Abelian transfer is direction-dependent and one-sided conclusions may require extra smoothed control.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This synthesis is internal to the specific arithmetic functions treated here and does not establish a general smoothing theorem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A shared explicit-formula pipeline controls zeta error and residue-class bias
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Both the zeta/Möbius error and the Dirichlet residue-class bias are transformed into sums over nontrivial zeros; symmetry or product bounds isolate a dominant low-zero or prime-square contribution, and coefficient decomposition returns the result to arithmetic.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The two applications use different zero-control devices and yield different directions of oscillation; the analogy should not erase those hypotheses.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Contour-shift failure becomes an explicit research criterion
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The Ramanujan-inspired reciprocal identity is not presented as proved: the source isolates a concrete horizontal-boundary estimate needed for the contour shift, generalizes the reciprocal transform, and then extracts a separate rigorously stated Riesz-growth criterion for RH.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The conjectural reciprocal formula and the proven RH criterion must remain distinct; scan damage also prevents exact formula reuse without source-image checking.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Stationary-phase analysis is reusable across zero sums and critical-line sign changes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A contour problem is converted to real oscillatory Dirichlet integrals, split into nonstationary tails and at most one resonant central index; the same phase-control technology later supplies the cancellation estimate needed for critical-line sign changes.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Exact phases and exponent balances are obscured by OCR and require scan verification before formal comparison.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Local sign changes produce a global critical-line zero lower bound
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source makes a real auxiliary function small on average, proves constant sign would force a conflicting main term, and concludes an odd-order zero in every sufficiently large short interval, which sums to a global lower bound.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This proves a lower bound for zeros on the line, not RH or a positive proportion of all zeros in the modern sense.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Phase alignment converts one seed asymptotic into recurring arithmetic extremes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A large value computed near the analytic boundary is reproduced at arbitrarily high locations by controlling the zero tail and simultaneously aligning finitely many phases; a boundary principle and explicit formula then turn it into recurring prime-counting extremes.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The mechanism is conditional on the source's RH reduction for this lower-bound proof and on exact spectral normalizations requiring scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Formal-worker warning: low-zero dominance and off-line-zero intuition need separate proofs
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source repeatedly distinguishes persuasive spectral intuition from proved control: low-zero dominance is rigorous only after a tail bound, while the expectation that an off-line zero overturns a conditional bias remains explicitly unproved.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a methodological synthesis, not a new theorem about either zeta or the Dirichlet L-function.

within_source_saturation: Saturated after a first-to-last-line audit of all ten source regions. Forty-seven units cover every distinct reusable mechanism, theorem interface, representation change, obstruction, failed route, and cross-section transfer recoverable from the normalized prose. Unselected material consists predominantly of title/citation/page furniture, blank transitions, routine intermediate algebra already represented by its governing mechanism, or formulas too extraction-damaged to support an additional independent unit. Exact symbolic reuse of many accepted units still requires the retained scan, as recorded unit by unit.
stop_reason: Stopped only after lines 1-4,267 were exactly partitioned and the remaining source material was accounted for: the introduction and all mathematical Sections 2-5 are represented through their distinct mechanisms and limitations; the final publication note adds no proof content, and the erratum concerns another paper. Further segmentation would mainly duplicate represented contour algebra, stationary-phase estimates, or routine summation details, or would isolate OCR-damaged displays without enough independent prose support.
